run.question: What are the statistics for the 'app-183g-stats' index? Tell me the document count, store size, and indexing rate.

report.summary: The 'app-183g-stats' index exists on the registered Elasticsearch target (target_id m0-otel-20260909), is open and green, and holds 50 live documents with 0 deleted. Primary and total store size are both reported as 8.5kb by _cat/indices, while _stats reports store.size_in_bytes 8754 (total_data_set_size_in_bytes 8754) and docs.total_size_in_bytes 8527. The indexing counters are cumulative since the index was created at 2026-11-23T17:17:50.964Z: index_total 50, index_current 0, index_failed 0, delete_total 0, noop_update_total 0, index_time_in_millis 1, is_throttled false. No true indexing rate (docs per second over a chosen interval) can be measured with the available tools: elasticsearch_index_stats and elasticsearch_list_indices have no time range and return only cumulative counters, and the index mapping has no date field, so documents themselves carry no timestamp to histogram. A rough lifetime average derived from the two observed facts is about 4.1 docs/s (50 docs indexed between creation and the snapshot ~12.2 s later), offered as an estimate, not a measured rate. Prometheus, which could in principle carry an Elasticsearch exporter metric, returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so that check could not be completed.

Index statistics for 'app-183g-stats': docs.count 50, docs.deleted 0, docs.total_size_in_bytes 8527; store.size_in_bytes 8754 and store.total_data_set_size_in_bytes 8754, identical in the primaries and total blocks (single primary shard, _shards successful 1 of 1, failed 0).

Indexing counters for 'app-183g-stats' are cumulative totals: index_total 50, index_time_in_millis 1, index_current 0, index_failed 0, index_failed_due_to_version_conflict 0, delete_total 0, noop_update_total 0, is_throttled false, throttle_time_in_millis 0, write_load 0.0001394200449346983; the same view reports refresh.total 3 and search.query_total 1 / fetch_total 1.

Both index tools state they have no time range and that their statistics counters are cumulative since node start or index creation, not counts inside the authorized window; the snapshot was observed at 2026-11-23T17:18:03Z, i.e. roughly 12 seconds after the index creation time 2026-11-23T17:17:50.964Z.

The mapping of 'app-183g-stats' contains only id (long), message (text with a keyword sub-field, ignore_above 256) and value (long); there is no date-mapped field, so the documents carry no timestamp that could be histogrammed to measure arrival rate.

Because index_total (50) equals docs.count (50) and the index was created at 2026-11-23T17:17:50.964Z, about 12.2 s before the 2026-11-23T17:18:03Z statistics snapshot, the lifetime average indexing throughput is roughly 4 docs/s. This is derived arithmetic from two observed values, not a measured rate over a chosen interval, and it assumes all 50 documents were indexed after creation and roughly evenly in that short span.

Indexing health signals do not show failures at snapshot time: index_failed 0, index_failed_due_to_version_conflict 0, delete_total 0, is_throttled false, throttle_time_in_millis 0, single segment (segments.count 1). This describes the index's own counters at one instant only and is not a statement about data correctness or about any period before it.

gaps: No measured indexing rate is available: elasticsearch_index_stats and elasticsearch_list_indices are snapshot/cumulative only (no time range), and the index has no date-mapped field, so a docs-per-second value over a defined interval cannot be computed from the available evidence.

The 8754-byte store figure and the 8.5kb _cat/indices figure are separate readings taken at slightly different moments (17:18:03Z); whether they are fully consistent after rounding is not verifiable, and neither proves historical size.

A Prometheus scrape of an Elasticsearch exporter that might expose an indexing-rate metric could not be checked: get_metric_names returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for target m0-otel-20260909, so it is unknown whether such a series exists.
change_history is not integrated in this Run, so no record of who or what created or modified this index is available.
next_steps: To obtain a real indexing rate, sample elasticsearch_index_stats (index.indexing.index_total for app-183g-stats) at two known times and divide the delta by the elapsed seconds, or have the application/indexing client expose a counter.
If per-document timing is needed, consider adding a date-mapped timestamp field to the index and re-checking a date_histogram over it.
Re-run the Prometheus metric discovery when the Prometheus source is reachable, to confirm whether an Elasticsearch exporter exposes indexing-rate series.
